title: Five metrics APIs, legible at a glance

anchors.1: coined jargon (fold, state, merge, close, strata, alias, collection, occurrence) or hidden setup
anchors.3: runs as shown and every name is imported, but two or three coined terms carry the meaning, or an output is a repr instead of a number or table
anchors.5: someone who has never seen the API reads only the glance and can say what each line does and what came out, without a single term defined. Every name is imported, the data's origin is shown, the verbs are ones a Python user knows (update / compute / reset, a plain function call, group_by / agg), and each output is a number with its unit or a small table

anchors.1: the rows are functions scattered over repos
anchors.3: a list exists, away from the part type
anchors.5: the part's metrics sit beside its models, each a configured stock metric with name, description, references and unit

anchors.1: per-run and roll-up are hand glue
anchors.3: per run is one call; roll-ups are hand-written
anchors.5: one call per recording, one for runs → rung → station → deployment, pooled vs per-run stated per metric

anchors.3: exact, but memory grows with the run
anchors.5: bounded memory, stops safe across chunk boundaries, time alignment handled or stated

anchors.3: metric + threshold, but owner or worst-vs-median hidden

def velocity_error_rms_deg_s(runs):
    """RMS of measured - target speed while the arm moves, in deg/s"""
    per_run = []
    for one_run in as_list(runs):
        moving = stock.moving(one_run.target)
        measured = one_run.measured.velocities[moving, 0]
        target = one_run.target.velocities[moving, 0]
        per_run.append(math.degrees(math.sqrt(np.mean((measured - target) ** 2))))
    return statistics.median(per_run)
